newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK short-term bill yields plunge on keen demand.
newsitem.headline: HK short-term bill yields plunge on keen demand.

text.p: Short-term Exchange Fund bill yields plunged on Thursday on keen demand for the paper from banks, widening the gap between bill yields and short-dated interbank offered rates to over 120 basis points, dealers said.
"Banks are buying for the start of RTGS since they cannot put their reputation at stake so they would rather buy more than what they may need," a U.S. bank dealer said.

The Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system will start operation on Monday. Under the RTGS, banks can use the bills to obtain interest-free intraday liquidity by carrying out intraday repo transactions with Hong Kong Monetary Authority.

One-week bill yields fell to 4.00 percent from 4.50 at Wednesday midday. One-month yielded 4.25 versus 4.57 and against average accepted yield of 4.44 percent on 28-day bills tendered earlier on Thursday. The one-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (HIBOR) stood at 5.74432 percent at 0300 GMT.

"Bill yields eased further after the tender result announcement and some Japanese banks were seen rushing to buy in late morning, probably they miscalculated the demand and made unsuccessful bids," a Japanese bank dealer said.
Roll-over purchases on some bills due today also amplified the buying, one trader said.
